rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ straying means that they associated partners with God.
rows.anchor: ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا} أشركوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first parsing, lā is extra: Aaron should have followed Moses’ command and fought the people’s unbelief as Moses would have.
rows.anchor: أن تتبعني و" لا " صلة أي تتبع أمري ووصيتي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as asking why Aaron did not join Moses and report the people’s deviation, so his separation would deter them.
rows.anchor: ما منعك من اللحوق بي وإخباري بضلالتهم، فتكون مفارقتك إياهم زجرا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had seized Aaron’s beard and head hair, specifically his forelocks.
rows.anchor: أي بشعر رأسي وكان قد أخذ ذوائبه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron feared that objecting would divide the Israelites into factions that fought one another, and Moses would blame him for splitting them.
rows.anchor: لو أنكرت عليهم لصاروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron says he feared Moses would say he had not kept the instruction to remain among the people and treat them gently.
rows.anchor: حين قلت لك اخلفني في قومي، وأصلح أي ارفق بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khatb asks what the matter or situation was, and what had prompted the deed.
rows.anchor: ما أمرك وشأنك؟ وما الذي حملك على ما صنعت؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan says he saw what the others did not see and understood what they did not know.
rows.anchor: رأيت ما لم يروا وعرفت ما لم يعرفوا.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamzah and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with second-person address, “you did not see”; the other readers have third-person “they did not see.”
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: " ما لم تبصروا " بالتاء على الخطاب،

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ reports that a guest came to the Prophet, who sent him to a Jewish man for flour on credit until Rajab; the man required collateral, so the Prophet sent his iron armor, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رافع: نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means not to look at what God has granted them for worldly enjoyment.
rows.anchor: لا تنظر، {إلى ما متعنا به} أعطينا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan here means kinds or classes among them.
rows.anchor: {إلى ما متعنا به} أعطينا، {أزواجا} أصنافا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “flower” of worldly life means its adornment and splendor.
rows.anchor: أي زينتها وبهجتها، وقرأ يعقوب زهرة بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads zahrah with fatḥa on the hāʾ; the general reading has sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب زهرة بفتح الهاء وقرأ العامة بجزمها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes their abundance a trial: He increases their blessing, and they respond with greater disbelief and transgression.
rows.anchor: بأن أزيد لهم النعمة فيزيدوا كفرا وطغيانا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s provision refers to Paradise in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: {ورزق ربك} في المعاد، يعني: الجنة،

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says that reliance on God prevents regret, fixation on others’ possessions prolongs grief, and measuring blessing by food, drink, and clothing leaves one with little work and imminent punishment.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب: من لم يتعز بعز الله تقطعت نفسه حسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your family” means your people; another view means those who share your religion, as in Maryam 19:55.
rows.anchor: أي قومك. وقيل: من كان على دينك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persist in prayer, since prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي اصبر على الصلاة، فإنها تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not charge the Prophet with providing for any creature or even himself; He charges him with work.
rows.anchor: لا نكلفك أن ترزق أحدا من خلقنا، ولا أن ترزق نفسك وإنما نكلفك عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides for the Prophet and the good end is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: {نحن نرزقك والعاقبة} الخاتمة الجميلة المحمودة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good, praiseworthy end belongs to the people of piety.
rows.anchor: الخاتمة الجميلة المحمودة، {للتقوى} أي لأهل التقوى.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the pious as those who affirm the Prophet, follow him, and fear God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الذين صدقوك واتبعوك واتقوني.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report in some Musnads says that when hardship struck his family, the Prophet would order them to pray and recite this verse.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض المسانيد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر أمرهم بالصلاة وتلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers ask for a proposed sign, although the Prophet had already brought many signs.
rows.anchor: {وقالوا} يعني المشركين، {لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه}

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Medina and Basra readers and Ḥafṣ read taʾtihim, feminine to agree with bayyinah; the others read yaʾtihim, with the verb preceding and agreeing semantically with “clarification.”
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص عن عاصم: " تأتهم " لتأنيث البينة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the Qur’an clarifies the earlier scriptures and is stronger in proof and clearer as a sign.
rows.anchor: أي بيان ما فيها، وهو القرآن أقوى دلالة وأوضح آية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that earlier scriptures recount nations who requested signs but did not believe when signs came; the Meccans may fare likewise.
rows.anchor: التوراة، والإنجيل، وغيرهما من أنباء الأمم أنهم اقترحوا الآيات، فلما أتتهم ولم يؤمنوا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened destruction would have come before sending a messenger and revealing the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: من قبل إرسال الرسول وإنزال القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people would plead on Judgment Day that a messenger should have been sent so they could follow God’s signs before humiliation and disgrace.
rows.anchor: هلا {أرسلت إلينا رسولا} يدعونا، أي: لقالوا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the lām as meaning “from,” so the reckoning has drawn near to people.
rows.anchor: قيل اللام بمعنى من، أي اقترب من الناس حسابهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The approaching reckoning is God’s accounting of people’s deeds on the Day of Resurrection; the verse was revealed about deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي وقت محاسبة الله إياهم على أعمالهم، يعني يوم القيامة، نزلت في منكري البعث،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of preparing for the reckoning.
rows.anchor: في غفلة معرضون} عن التأهب له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new reminder is each fresh revelation of the Qur’an that God sends to admonish them.
rows.anchor: يعني ما يحدث الله من تنزيل شيء من القرآن يذكرهم ويعظهم به.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil explains “new” as God bringing one matter after another.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يحدث الله الأمر [بعد الأمر]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the reminder as the Prophet’s sayings, Sunnah, and exhortations besides the Qur’an; it is attributed to God because he spoke by God’s command.
rows.anchor: قيل: الذكر المحدث ما قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبينه من السنن والمواعظ سوى ما القرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listen while playing, without reflection or accepting admonition.
rows.anchor: أي استمعوه لاعبين لا يعتبرون ولا يتعظون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are distracted, heedless, and turned away from God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: ساهية غافلة، {قلوبهم} معرضة عن ذكر الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective precedes its noun; in separation it takes accusative, as in Qamar 54:7 and Insan 76:11, while in connection it follows the noun’s case, as in Nisa 4:75.
rows.anchor: وإذا تقدم النعت الاسم فله حالتان: فصل ووصل، فحالته في الفصل النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who associated partners with God.
rows.anchor: {وأسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا} أي أشركوا،

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī finds fronting and delay: the intended order is “the wrongdoers held the secret counsel.”
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: فيه تقديم وتأخير، أراد: والذين ظلموا أسروا النجوى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes “those who” a nominative topic: they are the ones who held the secret counsel.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حمل "الذين" رفع على الابتداء، معناه: وأسروا النجوى، ثم قال: وهم الذين ظلموا.

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: A third parsing makes “those who” a substitute for the plural pronoun in “they held”; al-Mubarrad compares the construction with “the people in the house went out, the sons of ʿAbd Allāh.”
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: هذا كقولك إن الذين في الدار انطلقوا بنو عبد الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In their secret counsel, they object that a human like themselves has been sent and ask whether they should accept magic while seeing clearly.
rows.anchor: أنكروا إرسال البشر وطلبوا إرسال الملائكة.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read “We reveal” with nūn and kasra, matching “We sent”; the others read the passive “it is revealed” with yāʾ and fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم نوحي إليه بالنون وكسر الحاء على التعظيم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every messenger was taught that there is no god but God, so people must worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون} وحدون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Khuzāʿah, who claimed that the angels were God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: نزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا: الملائكة بنات الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God declares Himself exalted above the claim that He has a child.
rows.anchor: سبحانه} نزه نفسه عما قالوا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged offspring are angels, who are honored servants of God.
rows.anchor: أي هم عباد، يعني الملائكة، {مكرمون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not speak ahead of God or speak except as He commands.
rows.anchor: لا يتقدمونه بالقول ولا يتكلمون إلا بما يأمرهم به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels disobey God neither in word nor in deed.
rows.anchor: معناه أنهم لا يخالفونه قولا ولا عملا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God knows what the angels have done and what they will do.
rows.anchor: أي ما عملوا وما هم عاملون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God knows what preceded their creation and what follows it.
rows.anchor: ما كان قبل خلقهم وما يكون بعد خلقهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the angels intercede only for one who says “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي لمن قال لا إله إلا الله،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains the approved person as one with whom God is pleased.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أي لمن رضي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are fearful and do not feel secure against God’s plan.
rows.anchor: خائفون لا يأمنون مكره.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah says the threat refers to Iblīs, who called people to worship and obey him; no angel claimed divinity.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: عنى به إبليس حين دعا إلى عبادة نفسه وأمر بطاعة نفسه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who assign divinity and worship to what does not deserve them are wrongdoers punished with Hell.
rows.anchor: الواضعين الإلهية والعبادة في غير موضعها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: {واقترب الوعد الحق} يعني القيامة، قال الفراء

rows.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others treat the wāw as extra, so the promise draws near after Gog and Magog are released; they compare the wording with the wāw in Ṣāffāt 37:103.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء وجماعة: الواو في قوله واقترب [مقحمة فمعناه حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج اقترب] (2) الوعد الحق،

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: A report from Ḥudhayfah says that if someone acquired a young horse after Gog and Magog emerged, he would not ride it before the Hour.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن حذيفة قال: لو أن رجلا اقتنى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج لم يركبه حتى تقوم الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others reject dropping the wāw and make “Woe to us” the answer to ḥattā idhā: when Gog and Magog are released and the promise nears, they cry out.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: لا يجوز طرح الواو، وجعلوا جواب حتى إذا فتحت في قوله يا ويلنا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis takes “it” as a pronoun for the eyes, then repeats “eyes” for clarification.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أنها كناية عن الأبصار. ثم أظهر الأبصار بيانا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis treats “it” as a supporting pronoun, as in the construction cited from Hajj 22:46.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن "هي" تكون عمادا كقوله: {فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار} (الحج:46) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis ends the first clause at “it is,” meaning the event is present, then fronts the predicate: the unbelievers’ eyes are fixed.
rows.anchor: ثم ابتدأ: {شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا} على تقديم الخبر

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the disbelievers’ eyes are frozen open, scarcely blinking from the terror and horror of that day.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: شخصت أبصار الكفار فلا تكاد تطرف من شدة ذلك اليوم وهوله،

words: يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers lament that they had been heedless of that day; they admit they were wrongdoers by worshipping the wrong objects.
rows.anchor: يقولون، {يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا} اليوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who argued often, called angels God’s daughters and the Qur’an tales of the ancients, and denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: نزلت في النضر بن الحارث (4) كان كثير الجدل، وكان يقول: الملائكة بنات الله،

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّنَ الْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of human creation is offered as evidence against those who deny resurrection after becoming dust.
rows.anchor: وكان ينكر البعث وإحياء من صار ترابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marīd means rebellious and persistent in evil.
rows.anchor: والمريد: المتمرد المستمر في الشر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was decreed against the devil that whoever follows him will be led astray and guided to the punishment of the Blaze.
rows.anchor: كتب عليه} قضي على الشيطان، {أنه من تولاه} اتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first human, Adam, is meant by creation from dust; his descendants are meant by the subsequent stages.
rows.anchor: يعني: أباكم آدم الذي هو أصل النسل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfah is semen, literally a small quantity of water; its plural is nuṭāf.
rows.anchor: والنطفة هي المني، وأصلها الماء القليل وجمعها نطاف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ʿalaqah is thick, clotted blood; its plural is ʿalaq.
rows.anchor: وهي الدم الغليظ المتجمد، وجمعها علق،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop becomes thick blood and then flesh.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن النطفة تصير دما غليظا ثم تصير لحما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍghah is a small piece of flesh about the amount one could chew.
rows.anchor: وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما يمضغ،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah say mukhallaqah is fully formed and ghayr mukhallaqah is incomplete.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: "مخلقة" أي تامة الخلق، "وغير مخلقة" غير تامة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the terms mean shaped and unshaped, referring to a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مصورة وغير مصورة، يعني السقط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the formed one as a child delivered at term and the unformed one as a miscarriage.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "المخلقة" الولد الذي تأتي به المرأة لوقته، "وغير المخلقة" السقط.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that an angel takes the settled drop and asks God whether it is to be formed; if not, it is expelled as blood, and if so the angel records its sex, fortune, lifespan, deeds, provision, and place of death from the Mother Book.
rows.anchor: روي عن علقمة عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: إن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك بكفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages demonstrate the completeness of God’s power and wisdom in shaping creation and allow people to infer resurrection from the initial creation.
rows.anchor: كمال قدرتنا وحكمتنا في تصريف أطوار خلقكم ولتستدلوا بقدرته في ابتداء الخلق على قدرته على الإعادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God clarifies what people should do, avoid, and need for worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لنبين لكم ما تأتون وما تذرون وما تحتاجون إليه في العبادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps in the womb what He wills rather than letting it be expelled or miscarried, until the appointed time of complete birth.
rows.anchor: فلا تمجه ولا تسقطه، {إلى أجل مسمى} وقت خروجها من الرحم تامة الخلق والمدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭiflan is singular although the referent is plural because Arabic can use a singular noun for a group; another explanation likens it to verbal nouns such as ʿadl and zūr.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل: أطفالا لأن العرب تذكر الجمع باسم الواحد. وقيل: تشبيها بالمصدر مثل عدل وزور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashudd means full maturity and strength.
rows.anchor: ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم} يعني: الكمال والقوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die before reaching old age; others are returned to the most decrepit age, when their minds change and they know nothing after having known.
rows.anchor: من قبل بلوغ الكبر، {ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر} أي: الهرم والخرف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāmidah describes dry land without vegetation.
rows.anchor: هامدة} أي: يابسة لا نبات فيها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes the land move as plants rise; it lifts and grows. Another ordering is “grew and moved,” with “its vegetation” understood as omitted.
rows.anchor: تحركت بالنبات وذلك أن الأرض ترتفع بالنبات فذلك تحركها،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads rabaʾat with hamza, also in Fuṣṣilat, meaning that the land rose and became elevated.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: " وربأت " بالهمزة، وكذلك في حم السجدة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land produces every pleasing kind of plant, a delight to whoever sees it; this is another proof of resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي: صنف حسن يبهج به من رآه، أي: يسر، فهذا دليل آخر على البعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people, meaning Muslims, join the listed creatures in glorifying God.
rows.anchor: أي: من هذه الأشياء كلها تسبح الله عز وجل "وكثير من الناس"، يعني المسلمين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those for whom punishment is due are the disbelievers, who refuse prostration, although their shadows prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: وهم الكفار لكفرهم وتركهم السجود وهم مع كفرهم تسجد ظلالهم لله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw introducing the second “many” begins a new statement.
rows.anchor: والواو في قوله: {وكثير حق عليه العذاب} واو الاستئناف.

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God humiliates cannot be honored by anyone.
rows.anchor: أي: من يذله الله فلا يكرمه أحد، {إن الله يفعل ما يشاء}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God honors and humiliates as He wills; felicity and misery occur by His will and choice.
rows.anchor: أي: يكرم ويهين فالسعادة والشقاوة بإرادته ومشيئته.

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sābiṭ says that when pilgrims came to Mecca, no Meccan was more entitled to his own house than they were; ʿUmar forbade residents to shut their doors during the season.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن سابط: كان الحجاج إذا قدموا مكة لم يكن أحد من أهل مكة بأحق بمنزله منهم.

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: On the view associated with ʿUmar’s rule that residents could not restrict access during pilgrimage, selling or renting Meccan houses is impermissible.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب ينهى الناس أن يغلقوا أبوابهم في الموسم، وعلى هذا القول لا يجوز بيع دور مكة وإجارتها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī prefers the opposing view, which permits sale and lease: the verse attributes homes to their expelled owners, and reports show ownership and sale in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الأول -وهو الأقرب إلى الصواب -يجوز، لأن الله تعالى قال: {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم} (الحج: 40) ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet declared that whoever entered Abū Sufyān’s house was safe at the conquest of Mecca, attributing the house to its owner; ʿUmar also bought a Meccan house for a prison for four thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم فتح مكة: "من دخل دار أبي سفيان فهو آمن" (2) فنسب الدار إليه نسب ملك،

rows.speaker: طاووس وعمرو بن دينار والشافعي
rows.claim: Permitting sale of Meccan houses is the view of Ṭāwūs, ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, and al-Shāfiʿī.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول طاوس وعمرو بن دينار، وبه قال الشافعي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād means inclining toward wrongdoing in the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: أي: في المسجد الحرام بإلحاد بظلم وهو الميل إلى الظلم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī treats the bāʾ as extra, citing Muʾminūn 23:20 and al-Aʿshā’s use of bi-rizq to mean provision.
rows.anchor: قال الأعشى: "ضمنت برزق عيالنا أرماحنا"، أي: رزق عيالنا.

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects treating the bāʾ as extra: the meaning is that a person intends wrongdoing there.
rows.anchor: وأنكر المبرد أن تكون الباء زائدة وقال: معنى الآية من تكن إرادته فيه بأن يلحد بظلم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Qatādah identify ilḥād as associating partners with God and worshipping another deity.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد وقتادة: هو الشرك وعبادة غير الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view extends ilḥād to any forbidden word or deed, even insulting a servant.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: هو كل شيء كان منهيا عنه من قول أو فعل حتى شتم الخادم.

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ defines it as entering the sanctuary without iḥrām or committing its violations, such as hunting game or cutting trees.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: هو دخول الحرم غير محرم، أو ارتكاب شيء من محظورات الحرم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is killing someone who would not kill you or wronging someone who does not wrong you; al-Ḍaḥḥāk gives the same sense.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو أن تقتل فيه من لا يقتلك، أو تظلم فيه من لا يظلمك،

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also says sins are multiplied in Mecca just as good deeds are.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه قال: تضاعف السيئات بمكة كما تضاعف الحسنات.

rows.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
rows.claim: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit identifies the wrongdoing as hoarding food in Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال حبيب بن أبي ثابت: وهو احتكار الطعام بمكة.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a mere intention to sin is not recorded until acted upon, but intending to kill someone in Mecca, even while in Aden or elsewhere, brings painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله: {ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم} قال: لو أن رجلا هم بخطيئة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī adds that the threat does not apply if the person repents.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إلا أن يتوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who were expelled” is a substitute for the earlier “those” in the passage.
rows.anchor: {الذين أخرجوا من ديارهم بغير حق} بدل "عن الذين" الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were expelled from their homes for no reason except saying that God alone is their Lord.
rows.anchor: أي: لم يخرجوا من ديارهم إلا لقولهم ربنا الله وحده.

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s repelling of some people by others occurs through jihad and enforcement of legal penalties.
rows.anchor: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} بالجهاد وإقامة الحدود،

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The people of the Ḥijāz read the verb with a light dāl; the other readers double it, a form specific to extensive demolition.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز بتخفيف الدال، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد على التكثير،

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ hermitages.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك: يعني: صوامع الرهبان.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah identifies the ṣawāmiʿ as hermitages of the Ṣābiʾans.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: صوامع الصابئين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buyūʿ is the plural of biʿah, a Christian church.
rows.anchor: بيع النصارى جمع "بيعة" وهي كنيسة النصارى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish synagogues, called ṣalōtā in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: يعني كنائس اليهود، ويسمونها بالعبرانية صلوتا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosques are those of the Muslim community of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني مساجد المسلمين من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship places of each prophetic community would have been demolished in its own era: synagogues in Moses’ time, churches and hermitages in Jesus’ time, and mosques in Muhammad’s time.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض لهدم في شريعة كل نبي مكان صلاتهم،

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd instead identifies ṣalawāt as Muslim prayers, which would cease if an enemy entered upon them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أراد بالصلوات صلوات أهل الإسلام، فإنها تنقطع إذا دخل العدو عليهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will aid whoever aids His religion and His Prophet.
rows.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي: ينصر دينه ونبيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty and invincible.
rows.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي: ينصر دينه ونبيه، {إن الله لقوي عزيز}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes those empowered on earth as a description of God’s supporters; empowerment means victory over enemies until they control the land.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: هذا من صفة ناصريه، ومعنى "مكناهم في الأرض": نصرناهم على عدوهم حتى

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah identifies those empowered as the Companions of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هم أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies them as this Muslim community.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هم هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When empowered, they establish prayer, give alms, command right, and forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: أقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All created affairs end with God; every other sovereignty disappears, leaving Him without rival or claimant.
rows.anchor: أي: آخر أمور الخلق ومصيرهم إليه، يعني: يبطل كل ملك سوى ملكه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God as servants and as property.
rows.anchor: {له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض} عبيدا وملكا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of His servants and praiseworthy in His acts.
rows.anchor: عن عباده، {الحميد} في أفعاله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected what is on earth and ships to people; the ships are also understood as separately subjected to them.
rows.anchor: أي: وسخر لكم الفلك، {تجري في البحر بأمره}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes what is on land as riding animals and the ships as means of travel at sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "ما في الأرض": الدواب تركب في البر، و"الفلك" تركب في البحر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God holds the sky up so it does not fall onto earth, except by His permission.
rows.anchor: يعني: لكيلا تسقط على الأرض، {إلا بإذنه إن الله بالناس لرءوف رحيم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought people into existence when they were nothing.
rows.anchor: {وهو الذي أحياكم} أي: أنشأكم ولم تكونوا شيئا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes death when each person’s appointed term expires.
rows.anchor: {ثم يميتكم} عند انقضاء آجالكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will resurrect people for reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: {ثم يحييكم} يوم البعث للثواب والعقاب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is ungrateful for God’s blessings.
rows.anchor: {إن الإنسان لكفور} لنعم الله.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains mansakan as a religious law practiced by each community.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني شريعة هم عاملون بها.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives “festival” as another meaning of mansak.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قال: عيدا قال قتادة ومجاهد: موضع قربان يذبحون فيه.

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatādah and Mujāhid understand it as a place where sacrificial offerings are slaughtered.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ومجاهد: موضع قربان يذبحون فيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views take mansak as a place of worship or a familiar place people frequent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: موضع عبادة. وقيل: مألفا يألفونه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, mansak is a customary place for a good or bad act; pilgrimage rites are called manāsik because people repeatedly visit their sites.
rows.anchor: المنسك في كلام العرب: الموضع المعتاد لعمل خير أو شر، ومنه "مناسك الحج" لتردد الناس إلى أماكن أعمال الحج.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter in which they dispute is the rules for sacrificial animals.
rows.anchor: {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} يعني في أمر الذبائح. نزلت في بديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Budayl ibn Warqāʾ, Bishr ibn Sufyān, and Yazīd ibn Khunays, who challenged the Companions’ distinction between animals people killed and those God killed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في بديل بن ورقاء، وبشر بن سفيان، ويزيد بن خنيس قالوا لأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the form as “do not dispute with them”; reciprocal dispute ceases when one side stops, unlike a one-sided act such as striking.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: معنى قوله {فلا ينازعنك} أي: لا تنازعهم أنت، كما يقال: لا يخاصمك فلان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call people to belief in your Lord.
rows.anchor: {وادع إلى ربك} إلى الإيمان بربك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is upon straight guidance.
rows.anchor: وادع إلى ربك} إلى الإيمان بربك، {إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaws is the highest Garden; its explanation was given earlier in Sūrat al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: وهو أعلى الجنة قد ذكرناه في سورة الكهف (2)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants neither die nor leave Paradise.
rows.anchor: {هم فيها خالدون} لا يموتون ولا يخرجون،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A hadith says God created Adam, wrote the Torah, and planted Firdaws with His hand, then swore that habitual wine drinkers and dayyuths would not enter it.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الحديث: "أن الله تعالى خلق ثلاثة أشياء بيده: خلق آدم بيده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” means Adam’s offspring; al-insān is a generic singular that can refer to one or many.
rows.anchor: يعني: ولد آدم، و"الإنسان" اسم الجنس، يقع على الواحد والجمع،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says sulālah means the purest part of the water.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: السلالة صفوة الماء.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says sulālah means the descendants of Adam.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من بني آدم. وقال عكرمة:

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrimah says it is what flows from the back; Arabs also call semen sulālah and a child salīl or sulālah because each is drawn out.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو يسيل من الظهر، والعرب تسمي النطفة سلالة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clay is Adam’s clay, from which the human lineage developed.
rows.anchor: قوله: {من طين} يعني: طين آدم. والسلالة تولدت من طين خلق آدم منه.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī explains this as a sperm extracted from clay, with Adam meant by clay.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: من نطفة سلت من طين، والطين آدم عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes “the human” itself to mean Adam.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد من الإنسان هو آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the extracted substance from every kind of soil.
rows.anchor: وقوله: "من سلالة: أي: سل من كل تربة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is made into a sperm-drop.
rows.anchor: يعني الذي هو الإنسان جعلناه نطفة، {في قرار مكين} حريز،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure resting place is the womb, prepared to hold the drop until its term is complete.
rows.anchor: حريز، وهو الرحم مكن [أي قد هيئ] (4) لاستقرارها فيه إلى بلوغ أمدها.

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read the two bone references in the singular; the other readers use the plural because a person has many bones.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو بكر "عظما"، {فكسونا العظام} على التوحيد فيهما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says forty days separate each of the stages of creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بين كل خلقين أربعون يوما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God clothed the bones with flesh.
rows.anchor: فكسونا العظام لحما} أي ألبسنا،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والشعبي وعكرمة والضحاك وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Abū al-ʿĀliyah say the new creation is the breathing of the spirit into the person.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ومجاهد، والشعبي، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو العالية: هو نفخ الروح فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah identifies the new creation as the growth of teeth and hair.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: نبات الأسنان والشعر.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In a report through Ibn Jurayj, Mujāhid says the phrase means reaching full youth.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جريج عن مجاهد: أنه استواء الشباب.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the new creation means becoming male or female.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن قال: ذكرا أو أنثى.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-ʿAwfī reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that the phrase covers life’s changing states after birth, from first cry and nursing through movement, weaning, maturity, and later stages.
rows.anchor: وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس: أن ذلك تصريف أحواله بعد الولادة من الاستهلال إلى الارتضاع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves exaltation and praise, as He always has and always will.
rows.anchor: {فتبارك الله} أي: استحق التعظيم والثناء بأنه لم يزل ولا يزال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn means best of image-makers and estimators; in Arabic, khalq means estimation.
rows.anchor: {أحسن الخالقين} المصورين والمقدرين. و"الخلق" في اللغة: التقدير.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says people make things and God makes things, but God is the best maker; khāliq can mean maker.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يصنعون ويصنع الله والله خير الصانعين، يقال: رجل خالق أي: صانع.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the plural “creators” by noting that Jesus also creates, as stated in Āl ʿImrān 3:49; God is the best of creators.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: إنما جمع الخالقين لأن عيسى كان يخلق كما قال: "إني أخلق لكم من الطين" (آل عمران -49)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a doubled yāʾ, mayyit describes one who has not yet died but will die; the light form mayt describes one already dead, so it does not fit here.
rows.anchor: والميت -بالتشديد -والمائت الذي لم يمت بعد وسيموت، والميت -بالتخفيف -: من مات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction parallels the wording in Zumar 39:30, “You will die and they will die.”
rows.anchor: كقوله: "إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون" (الزمر -30) .
